### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via PLATFORM_TOOLS_BY_PACKAGE (symbol, a top-level const object))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3f61e4f8fb567160f839c3269ee95aa89ee4f1db` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e5e2de6357b81b762b023473b3bd277da878e1c9` — the merge of head `dd844a9d1cc303f19bd0aefbd8089eb48e74d2ee` into base `3f61e4f8fb567160f839c3269ee95aa89ee4f1db`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e5e2de6357b81b762b023473b3bd277da878e1c9 && git checkout e5e2de6357b81b762b023473b3bd277da878e1c9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3f61e4f8fb567160f839c3269ee95aa89ee4f1db dd844a9d1cc303f19bd0aefbd8089eb48e74d2ee && git checkout -B drift-repro 3f61e4f8fb567160f839c3269ee95aa89ee4f1db && git merge --no-ff dd844a9d1cc303f19bd0aefbd8089eb48e74d2ee

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3f61e4f8fb567160f839c3269ee95aa89ee4f1db
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3f61e4f8fb567160f839c3269ee95aa89ee4f1db` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `97f93b5503d18dc18d5c4dc24aa443ddc7f0f68c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-tool-names.ts + packages/spec/src/ai/skill.zod.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-ai-tool-references.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-ai-tool-references.test.ts, packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-tool-names.test.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-tool-bridge-safety-annotations.test.ts, ui/scripts/check-i18n-call-site-keys.mjs, ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/__tests__/toolLabels-locale-parity-7481.test.ts, ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/__tests__/toolLabels-sentences-12724.test.ts, ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/{ar,de,en,es,fr,ja,ko,pt,ru,zh}.ts, the two changesets, and cloud `packages/service-ai-studio/src/__tests__/platform-tool-names-conformance.test.ts` (the named consumer)

Rendered 2026-11-06T19:38Z on the schema face (`record-recognisers --template --paths` read the face off the PR's file list; `Served-tier: CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` is the tier it prescribed, not one forced). Read-only: the net diff `origin/main...97f93b55` (13 files, +35/−1), card #31020, cloud#3656, precedent `eca7cd2008` and the head's check-runs, read once. The dev's report and the seat's conclusions were not used; every judgment below was re-derived from the cited code.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Clause-②: no — right.** The question is whether a published accept set or public surface widens. The accept set for `skill.tools[]` is `packages/spec/src/ai/skill.zod.ts`: `z.array(z.string().regex(/^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*\*?$/))` — a free snake_case string, unchanged by this diff. The only consumer that validates against the list is `packages/lint/src/validate-ai-tool-references.ts` (`collectToolUniverse` = `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_TOOL_NAMES` ∪ `stack.tools[]` ∪ the `action_` family), and its one verdict, `ai-skill-tool-unresolved`, is **warning** severity by design (ADR-0078 advisory-first; the runtime "deliberately tolerates unresolved names"). So before this diff a skill naming `delete_package` was advised, not refused; after it, it is not advised. Nothing a published package refused is now accepted, no export is added or removed (`PLATFORM_PROVIDED_TOOL_NAMES` is the same `ReadonlySet` export with one more member). Same reading the precedent `eca7cd2008` recorded for +3/−1 names.
- **Consumers of the list, read off the code:** `@objectstack/lint` (`validate-ai-tool-references.ts`, the universe above); `@objectstack/mcp` (`mcp-server-runtime.ts` `worldAnnotation`: a registered name gets `openWorldHint: false` — a closed-world claim that is true of `delete_package`, which acts on the environment's own packages; and the two hand-held safety sets, pinned as a SUBSET of the registry by `mcp-tool-bridge-safety-annotations.test.ts`, so an addition cannot red them); the ui label suites `toolLabels-locale-parity-7481` (every registered name needs a non-empty label in all ten packs) and `toolLabels-sentences-12724` (no value equals the id or the title-caser's output); `ui/scripts/check-i18n-call-site-keys.mjs` names the registry as the `chatbot.tool.` vocabulary and defers the set check to the parity suite; and the named consumer, cloud's `platform-tool-names-conformance.test.ts`, which asserts **exact equality** between `PLATFORM_TOOLS_BY_PACKAGE['service-ai-studio']` and `SERVICE_AI_STUDIO_TOOL_DEFINITIONS`.
- **Metadata-protocol: none — right.** No authorable key, accepted value or type changes: the Zod accept set for `tools[]` is the regex string above, and no `packages/spec/authorable-surface/` shard moves in the diff (none is touched, and no other file in the repo mirrors the list — the grep for the sibling names outside the locales finds only the registry, the MCP sets and card tests, no generated artifact).
- **Registry edit holds.** `delete_package` sits in its sorted place (`delete_field` < `delete_package` < `describe_metadata`), snake_case, no cross-group collision, outside the `action_` family — the four invariants `platform-tool-names.test.ts` pins. The header docblock's maintenance contract (a new name needs its `chatbot.tool.` label in every pack) is met.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on both `@objectstack/spec` and `@object-ui/i18n` is right: `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch` whatever the commit type (ruling A), and the changeset gate's two cross-checks (`added` under `no`, `narrowed` without the arm) are not triggered. Both changesets carry both declaration lines at line start, as does the PR body. `Check Changeset` is green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Docblock accuracy against cloud#3656:** the group comment says `delete_package` "only stages the removal of a package built in the environment — a person confirms before anything is deleted". That matches the tool's semantics as cloud#3656 records them: in the chat it queues a pending action and the write happens only on confirm (the dispatcher re-gates and calls `protocol.deletePackage` with the actor); on the MCP door it queues nothing and points the person to Studio's existing person-confirmed Delete package dialog; it refuses marketplace installs, code packages and system/cloud scopes — "built in the environment" is the right scope word. Accurate.
- **Ten translations, read one by one against their siblings in the same block:** en "Delete a package" (differs from the title-caser's output, so the sentences pin holds); zh 「删除一个应用包」 — 应用包 is the word the zh block already uses for `create_package` 「新建一个应用包」, `get_active_package` 「确认当前应用包」, `list_packages` 「列出已有应用包」, so "app" vs "package" is consistent, not a drift; de "Ein Paket löschen" (siblings: "Ein Paket anlegen", "Ein Feld löschen"); es "Eliminar un paquete" ("Crear un paquete", "Eliminar un campo"); fr "Supprimer un paquet" ("Créer un nouveau paquet", "Supprimer le champ"); ja 「パッケージを削除する」 (「パッケージを新しく作成する」, 「項目を削除する」); ko 「패키지 삭제하기」 (「패키지 새로 만들기」, 「필드 삭제하기」); pt "Excluir um pacote" ("Criar um pacote", "Excluir um campo"); ru "Удалить пакет" ("Создать новый пакет", "Удалить одно поле"); ar "حذف حزمة" ("إنشاء حزمة جديدة", "حذف أحد الحقول"). All ten are real sentences in their language, each using the package noun its own block already uses, no placeholder, no English fallback, and each lands in the same alphabetical slot so the key sets stay equal across packs.
- **Precedent file set (`eca7cd2008`):** registry + ten locales + one spec changeset + one i18n changeset — matched. The precedent's `plugin-chatbot` / `app-shell` work was the record-write card itself, which this tool does not need here (a `packageRemoval` card renderer is filed separately per the cloud#3656 seat record). The one precedent file this PR did not touch that is NOT card work is `packages/lint/src/validate-ai-tool-references.test.ts` — see ④.
- **MCP safety sets:** `delete_package` is not added to `PLATFORM_DESTRUCTIVE_TOOL_NAMES`. Read against `safetyAnnotations`: a declared `requiresConfirmation` on the definition outranks the name, and an unlisted name gets no `destructiveHint`, which the SDK reads as its default `true` — the cautious reading. The sets are "deliberately partial" by their own docblock and `remove_sample_data` is absent too. Not a finding.
- **Pin ordering for the consumer (advisory, outside this PR):** cloud's conformance test asserts exact equality, so a cloud pin move that carries this registry must land together with or after cloud#3686's manifest, or the test flips red in the other direction.
- **Check-runs on `97f93b55`, read once:** green — Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Check PR Size, Spec property liveness, Lint · ESLint, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · CI/release/engine gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Type Check · source gates, Build UI Deps, Plan Test Core shards, Dogfood Regression Gate, Auto Label, Flag docs. **NOT MEASURED** (in progress at read time; not polled): Build Core, Test Core 1–8 and its gate, Type Check · workspace / · debt ledger / · consumer gates, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Type Check UI, Lint UI, Test UI 1–16 and its gate, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI. The PR body's locally NOT-MEASURED gates map to those pending jobs: `check:doc-formula-expressions`, `check:i18n` and `check:i18n-coverage` run in `Type Check · consumer gates`; `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:lean-entry-closure` in `Build Core`; the ui `scripts/` vitest in `Test UI`. None is yet covered by green CI; the queue guard holds the landing until every check is green, so this record does not stand in for them.

### ④ Design judgment

For the one `hits` file, read against the ruling it implements (cloud#3656's staged-only tool, blocked on this registry) and its first consumer (cloud's exact-equality conformance test): the change holds. The registry gains the name the consumer registers, the docblock says what the name does in the terms the tool actually honours, the label contract the registry's own header imposes is met in all ten packs, and the declarations match what the code's accept sets show.

- **should-fix — no lint pin for the addition.** Every prior registry addition pinned "accepted" in `packages/lint/src/validate-ai-tool-references.test.ts` with a control name beside it (#16512's five, #27002's two, and the precedent `eca7cd2008` for `create_record` / `update_record`), on the file's own rule: "The pin lives here, not beside the constant: refused and accepted are this rule's verdicts, and the list's own file can only pin its shape." This PR's spec changeset claims exactly that verdict ("a skill whose `tools[]` names `delete_package` resolves under ADR-0109 reference integrity") without a pin. The claim holds by construction (the universe is the registry's set), no gate reds, so this is not a FAIL — a one-case `it('resolves the service-ai-studio package removal (cloud#3656)')` with a near-name control (e.g. `delete_packages`) can land in a follow-up or on this branch before the queue.

No must-fix found.

Delta record rendered 2026-11-07T02:59Z, superseding the prior record on `97f93b5503` (comment 6693733275, PASS) for the head move `97f93b5503` → `dd844a9d1c`. Judged only the delta: the merge `e3724bd976` (origin/main `3f61e4f8fb` in; main renamed `zh.ts` → `zh-Hans.ts`, `pt.ts` → `pt-BR.ts` and added the generated `zh-Hant.ts`) and the follow-up `dd844a9d1c`. Read-only: `git diff origin/main...dd844a9d1c`, `git diff 3f61e4f8fb e3724bd976`, `git show dd844a9d1c`, the generator and its pin, and the head's check-runs once. Everything the prior record judged and the delta does not touch stands as recorded there.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The merge brought nothing of its own.** `git diff 3f61e4f8fb e3724bd976` is exactly the prior 13-file diff carried across the renames: registry (+4/−1 docblock, +1 name), the two changesets, and one `delete_package` line in each of `ar, de, en, es, fr, ja, ko, ru` plus `pt-BR.ts` (was `pt.ts`) and `zh-Hans.ts` (was `zh.ts`). No conflict-resolution content, no other file. The merge did NOT touch `zh-Hant.ts`, so at `e3724bd976` the generated pack lagged its source — which the follow-up fixes.
- **`delete_package` survived both renames in every pack.** Net diff against `origin/main` at `dd844a9d1c`: 11 packs each gain exactly one line — en "Delete a package", zh-Hans 「删除一个应用包」, zh-Hant 「刪除一個應用包」, pt-BR "Excluir um pacote", and ar/de/es/fr/ja/ko/ru unchanged from the prior record — each in its sorted slot after `delete_field`, so the key sets stay equal across packs (the parity and sentences suites now read the count off `PLATFORM_LOCALE_TAGS.length`, not a literal 10, so 11 packs is what they expect).
- **Registry unchanged by the delta:** `delete_package` still sits between `delete_field` and `describe_metadata`, docblock as before; net diff identical to the one reviewed on `97f93b5503`.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged: `patch` on `@objectstack/spec` and `@object-ui/i18n`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none` on both changesets and the PR body. The i18n changeset is reworded only ("in every pack" for "in all ten packs"; names the zh-Hant regeneration) — still right, and now accurate to the 11-pack set. `Check Changeset` is green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **zh-Hant line is generated, not hand-written, and correct.** `dd844a9d1c` changes two files: the changeset text and one line in `ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/zh-Hant.ts`. The file keeps its `// @generated by ui/packages/i18n/scripts/gen-zh-hant.mjs from ./zh-Hans.ts` header intact. The value 「刪除一個應用包」 is the OpenCC s2twp conversion of 「删除一个应用包」 character for character, and it agrees with what the converter already produced for the siblings in the same block — `create_package` 「新建一個應用包」, `get_active_package` 「確認當前應用包」, `list_packages` 「列出已有應用包」, `delete_field` 「刪除一個欄位」 — so 應用包 is the converter's word, not a hand choice. Byte-equality with the generator is pinned by `src/__tests__/zh-hant-generated.test.ts` (`committed === generate(read(source))` per target, plus the header check), which runs in the i18n suite under `Test UI` — in progress at read time, so the mechanical proof is NOT MEASURED here; the reading above is the read-only equivalent and finds nothing off.
- **Check-runs on `dd844a9d1c`, read once:** green — Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Check PR Size, Spec property liveness, Build Core, Build UI Deps, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Lint UI, Lint & Repo Gates, every `Lint ·` job (ESLint, repo & tooling, docs & code, CI/release/engine, PM dispatch-gates, scoped ×3), every `Type Check ·` job (source gates, workspace, debt ledger, consumer gates), TypeScript Type Check, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test Core 2/5/8, Test UI 2/12, Auto Label, Flag docs. **NOT MEASURED** (in progress; not polled): Type Check UI, Test Core 1/3/4/6/7 and its gate, Test UI 1/3–11/13–16 and its gate. The ui `scripts/` vitest and the zh-Hant generated pin stay with the pending `Test UI` shards; the queue guard holds the landing until they are green.

### ④ Design judgment

The delta is a mechanical carry across main's locale rename plus the regeneration that rename made owed; the `hits` file is byte-identical to the one judged PASS before, and the one new line is the generator's own output for the zh-Hans sentence already reviewed. Nothing in the delta changes the ruling-and-consumer reading of the prior record.
